newsitem.title: FRANCE: UAE has chosen F16, Rafale fighters -- newsletter.
newsitem.headline: UAE has chosen F16, Rafale fighters -- newsletter.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates has decided buy 50 F-16 combat aircraft from Lockheed Martin Corp and a mix of 30 aircaft from France's Dassault Aviation, a defense newsletter said on Thursday.

The French TTU newsletter said the decision was to be announced on the national holiday December 2, and confirmed at Abu Dhabi's IDEX arms show next March, but the authorities have already chosen. The deal is valued at about $6 billion.
The UAE will buy 18 Dassault Mirage 2000-5 and 12 Rafales, it said. No one was available for comment at Dassault, which is flying the Rafale at Britain's Farnborough airshow this week.
The UAE already flies a fleet of 36 Mirage 2000's.
A senior UAE official recently told Reuters the McDonnell Douglas Corp F15 had been dropped from the competition.
Abu Dhabi wants multi-role, long-range aircraft with superior air-to-air combat capability.
UAE President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan discussed defense matters when he met French President Jacques Chirac at the beginning of August. France has a defense pact with the UAE.

TTU reported that the UAE's leading arms procurement officer and armed forces chief of staff Sheikh Mohammed bin Zaid al-Nahayan flew to Washington last week to meet U.S. officials and discussed a strengthening of their defense treaty, along the lines of the French pact.
